U6-00582: A freed slave woman of Maymūnah was given a sheep in charity, and it died. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ passed by it and said:
"Why did you not take its hide, tan it, and benefit from it?"
They said, "It is carrion." He said:
Abū Bakr and Ibn Abī ʿUmar said in their report, on the authority of Maymūnah, may Allah be pleased with her:
U6-01446: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Respond to this invitation when you are invited to it."
He said: ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿUmar would attend invitations, whether to a wedding feast or otherwise, and he would attend even when he was fasting.
U6-01323: Ibn ʿAbbās used to say, "No one who circumambulates the House, whether a pilgrim or not, [does so] except that he comes out of ihram."

I asked ʿAṭāʾ, "From where does he say that?" He said, "From the saying of Allah, the Exalted: {Then their place of sacrifice is at the Ancient House.}" I said, "But that is after [the standing at] ʿArafah."
He said, "Ibn ʿAbbās used to say it is after ʿArafah and before it."
He took that from the command of the Prophet ﷺ when he ordered them to come out of ihram during the Farewell Hajj.
U6-00321: Muʿādh used to pray with the Prophet ﷺ and then go and lead his people in prayer. One night he prayed the ʿIshāʾ prayer with the Prophet ﷺ, then went to his people and led them, beginning with Sūrat al-Baqarah. A man left the line, gave the salām, then prayed by himself and departed. They said to him, "Have you become a hypocrite, so-and-so?" He said, "No, by Allah! I will certainly go to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and tell him."

He came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said, "O Messenger of Allah, we are people who work with water-carrying camels, labouring by day. Muʿādh prayed ʿIshāʾ with you, then went and began with Sūrat al-Baqarah."
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ turned to Muʿādh and said:
"O Muʿādh, are you a cause of trial? Recite such-and-such and such-and-such."
Sufyān said: I said to ʿAmr, "Abū az-Zubayr narrated to us from Jābir that he said:
'Recite: By the sun and its brightness, and: By the morning brightness,
and: By the night when it covers,
and: Glorify the name of your Lord, the Most High.'"
U6-00895: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent us out, three hundred riders, with Abū ʿUbaydah ibn al-Jarrāḥ as our commander, to watch for a caravan of Quraysh. We stayed by the coast for half a month and were struck by severe hunger, so that we ate leaves of the khabaṭ tree, and so we were called the Army of the Khabaṭ. Then the sea cast up for us an animal called al-ʿanbar, and we ate from it for half a month and rubbed ourselves with its fat until our bodies recovered. He said: Abū ʿUbaydah took one of its ribs and stood it upright, then looked for the tallest man in the army and the tallest camel, and mounted him on it, and he passed beneath it. He said: A group of men sat in the socket of its eye. He said: And we took out of the hollow of its eye so many jars of fat. He said: We had with us a bag of dates, and Abū ʿUbaydah would give each man of us a handful, then he gave us one date each, and when it ran out we felt its loss.
U6-01474: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to the couple who had exchanged oaths of condemnation:
"Your reckoning is with Allah. One of you is lying. You have no claim over her."
He said, "O Messenger of Allah, what about my property?" He said:
"You have no property. If you told the truth about her, it is in return for having made her lawful to you; and if you lied about her, that is even further from you."
Zuhayr said in his narration: Sufyān narrated to us from ʿAmr, who heard Saʿīd ibn Jubayr say: I heard Ibn ʿUmar say: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
U6-01149: I sat with Abū Hurayrah for five years, and I heard him narrate
from the Prophet ﷺ, who said:
"The Children of Israel were governed by prophets;
whenever one prophet died, another succeeded him.
But there will be no prophet after me,
and there will be caliphs, and they will be many."
They said, "What do you command us?" He said, "Fulfil the pledge of allegiance to the first, then the next. Give them their due,
for Allah will question them about what He entrusted to their care."
U6-01524: A man came to the Prophet ﷺ and said, "My brother has a loose stomach."
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, "Give him honey to drink."
He gave it to him, then came back and said, "I gave him honey, and it only increased his diarrhea."
He told him this three times. Then he came the fourth time, and he said, "Give him honey to drink."
He said, "I did give it to him, but it only increased his diarrhea."
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Allah has spoken the truth, and your brother's stomach has lied." So he gave it to him and he was cured.
U6-01421: Three men came to the houses of the wives of the Prophet ﷺ asking about the worship of the Prophet ﷺ. When they were told, they seemed to regard it as little, and said, "Where are we compared to the Prophet ﷺ? Allah has forgiven him his earlier and later sins."
One of them said, "As for me, I will pray at night forever."
Another said, "I will fast continually and never break my fast."
Another said, "I will keep away from women and never marry."
Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ came and said,
"Are you the ones who said such and such? By Allah, I am the one among you who fears Allah most and is most mindful of Him,
yet I fast and I break my fast,
I pray and I sleep, and I marry women.
So whoever turns away from my Sunnah is not of me."
U6-00145: The Prophet ﷺ used to go around to his wives in a single hour of the night or day,
He said: I asked Anas, "Was he able to do that?" He said, "We used to say that he had been given the strength of thirty."
And Saʿīd said, from Qatādah, that Anas narrated to them that they were nine women.
U6-01342: from among the hypocrites in the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, whenever the Prophet ﷺ went out on a military expedition, would stay behind and rejoice at remaining behind the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. When the Prophet ﷺ returned, they would make excuses to him and swear oaths, and they loved to be praised for what they had not done. Then it was revealed: {Do not think that those who rejoice in what they have done and love to be praised for what they have not done—do not think they are safe from the punishment.}
U6-00029: A man from the Jews came to ʿUmar and said, "Commander of the Faithful, there is a verse in your Book that you recite; if it had been revealed to us, the community of Jews, we would have taken that day as a festival."

He said, "Which verse?" He said, {This day I have perfected for you your religion and completed My favor upon you and approved for you Islam as your religion.} ʿUmar said, "I know the day on which it was revealed and the place where it was revealed: it was revealed to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ at ʿArafāt on a Friday."
U6-01032: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ never veiled himself from me since I became Muslim, and he never saw me without smiling at me.
Ibn Numayr added in his narration from Ibn Idrīs: "I complained to him that I could not stay firm on horses, so he struck my chest with his hand and said,
'O Allah, make him firm, and make him one who guides and is rightly guided.'"
U6-00570: Some people of the Anṣār asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he gave every one of them who asked, until what he had was exhausted. When everything he had had been spent by his hands, he said to them,
"Whatever good I have, I will not withhold it from you.
Whoever seeks to be chaste, Allah will make him chaste.
Whoever strives to be patient, Allah will make him patient.
Whoever seeks to be self-sufficient, Allah will make him self-sufficient.
And you will never be given any gift better and more expansive than patience."
U6-01217: ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb was placed on his bier, and the people gathered around him, supplicating, praising him, and praying over him before he was lifted, and I was among them. He said: Suddenly I was startled by a man who took hold of my shoulder from behind. I turned to him, and it was ʿAlī. He asked Allah's mercy for ʿUmar and said, "You have left behind no one whom I would rather meet Allah with the like of his deeds than you. By Allah, I used to think that Allah would place you with your two companions, because I often heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say,
'I went, and Abū Bakr and ʿUmar; I entered, and Abū Bakr and ʿUmar; I left, and Abū Bakr and ʿUmar.'
So I hoped, or I thought, that Allah would place you with them both."
U6-00515: Saʿd ibn ʿUbādah fell ill with an illness, so the Prophet ﷺ came to visit him, together with ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf, Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ, and ʿAbdullāh ibn Masʿūd, may Allah be pleased with them. When he entered, he found him surrounded by his family and said, "Has he passed away?"
Then the Prophet ﷺ wept, and when the people saw the Prophet ﷺ weeping, they wept. He said,
"Do you not hear? Allah does not punish for the tears of the eye,
nor for the grief of the heart,
but He punishes for this"—and he pointed to his tongue—"or He shows mercy. And the dead is punished for the weeping of his family over him."
ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with him, used to strike with a stick over this,
throw stones, and throw dust [at those who wailed].
U6-00421: one of the Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. He said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ went out one day to pray for rain. He turned his back to the people, supplicating Allah and facing the qiblah, and he turned his cloak over, then he prayed two rakʿahs.
U6-01583: asked permission to see the Prophet ﷺ, and when he saw him he said: "
What a bad brother of the tribe,
and what a bad son of the tribe!"
Then when the man sat down, the Prophet ﷺ was cheerful toward him and was welcoming to him.
When the man left, ʿĀʾishah said to him: O Messenger of Allah, when you saw the man you said such and such about him,
then you were cheerful toward him and welcoming to him. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "
O ʿĀʾishah, when have you ever known me to be vulgar?
Indeed, the worst of people in rank with Allah on the Day of Resurrection is the one whom people leave alone out of fear of his evil."
U6-01927: Ḥujr. Yaḥyā ibn Yaḥyā said: Ismāʿīl informed us, and the others said: Ismāʿīl narrated to us,
who is Ibn Jaʿfar, from ʿAbdullāh ibn Dīnār,
say: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "
Whoever keeps a dog, other than a hunting dog or a herding dog, two qīrāṭs are deducted from his deeds every day."
U6-01944: to Kaʿb al-Aḥbār that the Prophet of Allah ﷺ said: "
Every prophet has a supplication that he makes, and I wish, if Allah wills, to keep my supplication in reserve as an intercession for my community on the Day of Resurrection."
Kaʿb said to Abū Hurayrah: Did you hear this from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ? Abū Hurayrah said: Yes.
U6-01945: from the Prophet ﷺ that he said: "
A servant's supplication continues to be answered as long as he does not pray for something sinful or for severing family ties, and as long as he does not become impatient."
It was said: O Messenger of Allah, what is impatience? He said: "
He says: 'I have supplicated and supplicated, but I have not seen [Him] answer me,' so he becomes worn out at that point and gives up supplication."
U6-01892: Saʿīd said: There was something between Khālid ibn al-Walīd and ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf, and Khālid insulted him. So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "
Do not insult any of my Companions, for if one of you were to spend gold equal to Uḥud, it would not reach a mudd of one of them, nor even half of it."
U6-01810: Prayer in the mosque of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ is better than a thousand prayers in any other mosque, except the Sacred Mosque, for the Messenger of Allah ﷺ is the last of the prophets, and his mosque is the last of the mosques.

Abū Salamah and Abū ʿAbdullāh said: We had no doubt that Abū Hurayrah was saying this from the words of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, but that kept us from asking Abū Hurayrah to confirm that hadith. When Abū Hurayrah died, we discussed it and blamed one another for not having spoken to Abū Hurayrah about it so that he would trace it to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, if he had heard it from him. While we were in that state, we sat with ʿAbdullāh ibn Ibrāhīm ibn Qāriẓ and mentioned that hadith and our shortcoming regarding Abū Hurayrah's explicit attribution of it. ʿAbdullāh ibn Ibrāhīm said to us: I bear witness that I heard Abū Hurayrah say: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "
I am the last of the prophets, and my mosque is the last of the mosques."
U6-01828: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ only hastened around the House and between aṣ-Ṣafā and al-Marwah in order to show the polytheists his strength.
Al-Ḥumaydī added: Sufyān narrated to us, ʿAmr narrated to us, I heard ʿAṭāʾ,
U6-01942: While we were traveling with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ at al-ʿArj, a poet appeared reciting verses. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "
Seize the devil," or "Hold back the devil. For a man's belly to be filled with pus is better for him than for it to be filled with poetry."
U6-01804: Hardship [a drought] struck the people during the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. While the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was delivering the sermon from the pulpit on Friday, a Bedouin stood up and said, "O Messenger of Allah,
the livestock are dying and the families are starving,
so pray to Allah for us to send us rain."
He said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ raised his hands,
though there was not a trace of cloud in the sky.
He said: Then clouds rose up like mountains,
and he had not yet come down from his pulpit when I saw the rain running down his beard.
He said: So it rained on us that day,
and the next day, and the day after, and the one following, until the next Friday.
Then that Bedouin or another man stood up and said, "O Messenger of Allah,
the buildings have collapsed and the livestock have drowned,
so pray to Allah for us."
So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ raised his hands and said:
"O Allah, around us and not upon us."
He said: Whenever he pointed with his hand toward a part of the sky, it cleared, until Madinah became like a hollow [surrounded by clouds],
and the valley, Wādī Qanāh, flowed for a month.
He said: And no one came from any direction except that he spoke of the abundant rain.
U6-01910: ʿAbdullāh ibn Ubayy ibn Salūl used to say to a slave girl of his, "Go and earn something for us [through prostitution]." So Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, revealed: {Do not force your young women into prostitution, if they wish to remain chaste, in order to seek the goods of worldly life. And whoever forces them, then indeed Allah, after their being forced,} to them {is Forgiving and Merciful.}
U6-01871: Anas ibn Mālik narrated to us from Abū Ṭalḥah,
that on the day of Badr the Prophet of Allah ﷺ ordered that twenty-four men of the leaders of Quraysh be thrown into one of the wells of Badr, a foul and filthy one.
And whenever he overcame a people, he would stay in their open ground for three nights.
So when it was the third day at Badr,
he ordered his mount, and its saddle was fastened on it.
Then he set out walking, and his Companions followed him, saying, "We think he is going only for some need of his,"
until he stood at the edge of the well.
He began calling them by their names and their fathers' names:
and O so-and-so, son of so-and-so,
would it please you that you had obeyed Allah and His Messenger? For we have found what our Lord promised us to be true,
so have you found what your Lord promised you to be true?"
He said: ʿUmar said, "O Messenger of Allah,
how can you speak to bodies that have no souls?" The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"By the One in whose hand is the soul of Muḥammad,
you do not hear what I say any better than they do."
Qatādah said: Allah brought them back to life so that they might hear his words, as a rebuke, a humiliation, a retribution, and a cause of regret and remorse.
U6-05497: Qays [Fāṭimah bint Qays] said: Tamīm al-Dārī came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and told the Messenger of Allah ﷺ that he had sailed the sea and his ship had gone astray, so he was cast up on an island. He went out onto it looking for water and met a person dragging his hair.
And he related the hadith, and in it he said: Then he said, "Had I been permitted to leave, I would have trodden all the lands except Ṭaybah."
So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ brought him out to the people and he told them. He said:
"This is Ṭaybah, and that is the Dajjāl."
U6-02007: We went out with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ to Khaybar.
When we were at al-Ṣahbāʾ, which Yaḥyā said is about an afternoon's journey from Khaybar, he called for food, but only barley meal was brought.
We chewed it and ate with him.
Then he called for water and rinsed his mouth, and we rinsed ours with him.
Then he led us in the Maghrib prayer without performing ablution anew.
Sufyān said: It is as if you were hearing it from Yaḥyā.
U6-05152: Al-Bunānī and Sulaymān al-Taymī, from Anas ibn Mālik,
that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"I came upon Mūsā, and in the narration of Haddāb, I passed by Mūsā, on the night I was taken on the Night Journey, at the red sand dune, while he was standing in prayer in his grave."
U6-02184: "O Allah, bless us in our Shām,
O Allah, bless us in our Yemen."
They said, "And in our Najd." He said:
"O Allah, bless us in our Shām,
O Allah, bless us in our Yemen."
They said, "O Messenger of Allah, and in our Najd?" I think he said the third time:
and from there the horn of Satan will rise."
U6-02549: The Prophet ﷺ said: "The best of you are my generation,
then those who come after them,
then those who come after them."
ʿImrān said: I do not know whether the Prophet ﷺ mentioned two generations or three after his own. The Prophet ﷺ said:
"After you will come a people who betray and are not trusted, who bear witness
without being asked to testify, who make vows and do not fulfil them,
and obesity will become apparent among them."
U6-04808: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"No raiding party fights in the cause of Allah and gains spoils except that they have hastened two-thirds of their reward in this world, and one-third remains for them in the Hereafter. And if they do not gain spoils, their reward is completed for them."
U6-02108: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Listen and obey, even if an Abyssinian slave whose head is like a raisin is appointed over you."
U6-03315: With this [chain], and she said: The Prophet ﷺ came to me one day and said:
"ʿĀʾishah, I do not think that so-and-so and so-and-so know anything of our religion, the one we follow."
U6-02059: went out from the presence of the Prophet ﷺ on a dark night,
and there was a light before them both, until they parted,
and the light parted with them.
And Maʿmar said, from Thābit, from Anas, that Usayd ibn Ḥuḍayr and a man from the Anṣār
U6-03219: I was a guest of Abū Hurayrah for seven days,
and he, his wife, and his servant would divide the night into three parts in turns: one would pray,
And I heard him say: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ distributed dates among his Companions,
and I received seven dates, one of which was a hard, dried-up date.
U6-04117: His son had died at Qudayd or ʿUsfān, and he said: "Kurayb, see how many people have gathered for him."
He said: I went out and found people had gathered for him, and I told him. He said: "Do you say they are forty?" He said: Yes.
U6-04668: When revelation came down upon the Prophet of Allah ﷺ, he would be distressed by it and his face would change color. He said: One day it was revealed to him and he was in that state. When it was lifted from him, he said:

"Take from me. Allah has made a way for them: the non-virgin with the non-virgin, and the virgin with the virgin. For the non-virgin, a hundred lashes and then stoning with stones; and for the virgin, a hundred lashes and then banishment for a year."
U6-05232: From the Prophet ﷺ, that he said this a month or so before his death:
"There is no living soul today upon which a hundred years will come while it is still alive."
the keeper of the water supply, from Jābir ibn ʿAbdullāh,
from the Prophet ﷺ, similar to that. ʿAbd al-Raḥmān explained it, saying: it means the shortening of lifespan.
U6-03752: I prayed with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, Abū Bakr, ʿUmar and ʿUthmān, and I did not hear any of them recite "In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful."
U6-05208: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Satirize the Quraysh, for it is harsher on them than a volley of arrows."
So he sent for Ibn Rawāḥah and said, "Satirize them."

He satirized them but it did not please him. Then he sent for Kaʿb ibn Mālik, then he sent for Ḥassān ibn Thābit. When he came to him, Ḥassān said: "The time has come for you to send for this lion who strikes with his tail." Then he stuck out his tongue and began to move it, and said: "By the One who sent you with the truth, I will tear them apart with my tongue as leather is torn."
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
"Do not be hasty, for Abū Bakr is the most knowledgeable of the Quraysh about their lineages, and I have kinship among them, until he distinguishes my lineage for you."

So Ḥassān went to him, then returned and said: "Messenger of Allah, he has distinguished your lineage for me. By the One who sent you with the truth, I will draw you out from among them as a hair is drawn out of dough."
U6-05538: ʿĀʾishah said to me: "My nephew, they were commanded to ask forgiveness
for the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ, yet they reviled them."
U6-03922: Our homes were far from the mosque,
our houses and move closer to the mosque, but the Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade us and said:
"For every step you take, you have a rank."
U6-03784: The Prophet ﷺ led us in the dawn prayer in Makkah and began reciting Sūrat al-Muʾminūn, until the mention of Moses and Aaron, or the mention of Jesus (Muḥammad ibn ʿAbbād was unsure, or they differed about it from him), when a cough seized the Prophet ﷺ, so he bowed. ʿAbdullāh ibn al-Sāʾib was present at that.
In the narration of ʿAbd al-Razzāq: he cut it short and bowed.
And in his narration: and ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAmr.
